identity.name: TrackMan Intelligence
identity.goal: Drive fitting bookings and coaching sessions

visualDirection.mood: Clinical precision. Data权威. TrackMan blue dominance.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: TrackMan data is the hero. Numbers, charts, launch monitor visuals. Chrome golf clubs on dark backgrounds. PGA Tour stat comparisons. Clean, scientific, premium. Think golf analytics lab meets luxury sports brand.
imageReferences: TrackMan launch monitor screen with ball flight data
Chrome iron head with data overlay (TrackMan numbers)
Golfer swing capture with split-screen stat comparison
Dark background, premium equipment photography
visualDirection.colorUsage: Use TrackMan blue (#0066CC) as dominant brand colour. Green (#00CC77) for positive metrics and CTAs. Gold for pricing. Never use for backgrounds — text only. Keep dark backgrounds consistent.
visualDirection.typography: Roboto Condensed Bold for numbers and headlines. Inter for body. Monospace for data labels.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Split screen: product/club on left, TrackMan data overlay on right. Dark backgrounds throughout. Numbers should dominate the visual hierarchy.
contentExamples: Your drive: 217m. PGA Tour avg: 264m. TrackMan found the gap.
Launch monitor screenshot showing spin rate + carry distance
Before/after swing data comparison

brief.purpose: Drive fitting bookings and coaching sessions by proving Swing Shack's TrackMan technology gives golfers data-driven insight their game has been missing.
brief.audience: Jozi golfers, 25-50, mid-high handicap. They track their fitness — they want to track their golf. Data-aware, skeptical of voodoo tips, willing to pay for evidence-based improvement.
brief.bigIdea: Your swing has a number. TrackMan measures it. That number is the shortcut to better scores.
brief.successMetric: Fitting sessions booked. Secondary: GMB posts live weekly. Tertiary: engagement rate on stat-hook content above 2.5%.
brief.whatGoodLooksLike: A hook that stops the scroll with a specific number. A visual that shows TrackMan data overlaid on a club or swing. A caption that earns the click by expanding the data story. Booking link front and centre.
brief.whatBadLooksLike: Vague transformation claims ('From confused golfer to confident striker'). Busy backgrounds without contrast. Price-led content without data justification. Anything that looks like generic golf marketing.

dna.tone: Clinical authority. Data speaks, we just translate it. No hype, no fluff — numbers are the argument. Authoritative but not cold. Expert without being gatekeeping.
dna.contentMix: 70% educational (data insights, stats explainers) / 20% promotional (session offers, fitting deals) / 10% social proof (client results, before/after)
forbiddenVisualStyles: text over busy backgrounds without contrast layer
dna.ctaPhilosophy: Direct price-led with anchoring: show the value first (TrackMan data), then introduce the offer. Always include R-amount. 'From R250' works because the data has already justified the price.

platformStrategy.instagram: Stat-first hook stops the scroll. Data overlay on image tells the story. Caption expands with context. Link in bio drives booking.
platformStrategy.tiktok: Hook is the number/stat itself. 'Your drive: 199m' as text overlay. 3-second hook, then explain the data. Fast-cut, punchy.
platformStrategy.gmb: Trust + proof + convenience. Service highlight with one key stat. Clean, professional, no gimmicks. Call to action is always 'book now' or 'call us'.

exampleHighPerforming.whyItWorked: 'Your golf stats don't lie' — specific, implies measurement, triggers curiosity about what the stats reveal. Stats hooks 2.5x better than transformation hooks.

exampleLowPerforming.whyItFailed: 'FROM CONFUSED GOLFER TO CONFIDENT STRIKER' — vague, no data anchor. Transformation claims without proof feel empty.

bestHooks.notes: Stats angle consistently outperforms transformation. 'Your [metric]' format is the winner.

failedContent.reason: Vague transformation claim, no data anchor
failedContent.lesson: Always lead with a number or specific stat. 'Your [X]' outperforms 'FROM [state] TO [state]'
Weather/indoor convenience is table stakes, not a hook. Stats create urgency.

lessonsLearned: Stats hooks consistently outperform all other angles — lead with numbers always
Meters > Yards for SA market — confirmed April 2026
Dark background with data overlay looks premium with TrackMan theme
Caption ≠ Overlay Text — supplementary copy drives click-through, not the hook itself
Hook A best performer (Round 1) was never re-published — opportunity cost

brief.purpose: Establish Takomo 101T as the smart golfer's iron of choice in SA — premium hollow-body technology at a price that challenges the big brands.
brief.audience: Serious golfers, 25-50, mid-to-low handicap. They do their research. They want Tour-level performance without Tour-level prices. They read reviews, compare specs, and buy based on data not branding.
brief.bigIdea: Takomo 101T: the iron that gets serious golfers arguing — and fitting sessions that settle the argument.
brief.successMetric: Takomo fitting sessions booked. Secondary: engagement on Takomo content above TrackMan benchmark. Tertiary: Takomo mentions in bio link clicks.
brief.whatGoodLooksLike: A real Takomo iron head on pure black — no AI, no stock photos. A price callout in gold that creates urgency without discounting. A hook that poses a question serious golfers want answered. Copy that respects the reader's intelligence.
brief.whatBadLooksLike: AI-generated club heads that look fake. Broken/garbled text. Price claims without the 'under $600' anchor. Generic golf content that could be any iron. Anything that talks down to the audience.

dna.tone: Confident, curious, slightly provocative. The kind of content that makes serious golfers stop and think — then book a fitting to settle the argument. Sharp without being aggressive.
dna.contentMix: 50% product education (what makes Takomo different) / 30% controversy/question angle / 20% value proof (price-to-performance)

dna.ctaPhilosophy: Price transparency as hook: lead with 'less than $600' or 'from R250' because the value is the argument. CTAs are always 'Book Takomo Fitting' with R-amount anchored.

platformStrategy.instagram: Product-first: the iron head IS the hero. Price callout in gold. Caption earns the click with the controversy/question angle. Link to booking.
platformStrategy.tiktok: Hook is the price question: 'Is Takomo 101T worth it? We put it on TrackMan.' Product visual first, data second.
platformStrategy.gmb: Takomo fitting service highlight. Price-led. Trust signal: 'Swing Shack is authorized Takomo fitter.'

exampleLowPerforming.whyItFailed: AI-generated club head looked fake. Text broken/garbled. Pricing callout wrong. Product credibility too low. Real product photography required per Christelle gate rule.

failedContent.reason: AI product imagery looks fake. Broken text. Wrong pricing. Product credibility too low.

identity.name: Winter Golf
identity.goal: Drive indoor golf sessions during SA winter season

visualDirection.mood: Cozy indoor warmth vs cold outside. Jozi winter contrast. Indoor golf paradise.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Cold outside, warm inside. The contrast between grey Jo'burg winter and the warmth, green satisfaction of indoor golf. Pizzas, beers, premium simulators. Social golf atmosphere. NOT about technique or data — about the experience and enjoyment. Think: pub golf meets luxury simulator.
imageReferences: Simulator screen showing lush course in winter grey context
Cozy indoor setup with warm lighting
Post-round drinks at Swing Shack bar
Rain on window outside, golfer smiling inside
visualDirection.colorUsage: Cool blues for winter theme (#4A90D9). Warm accent for indoor coziness (#D4A574 or warm amber). Never clinical — keep it inviting and social.
visualDirection.typography: Warm, approachable. Bold for contrast headlines. Friendly sans-serif.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Split mood: grey/cold outside vs warm/green inside. Social proof. Food and beverage welcome. Not data-heavy.
contentExamples: It's 8°C outside. 22°C inside. Your game never stops.
Rain check? How about a round.
Winter doesn't exist in here.

brief.purpose: Keep Swing Shack bookings steady through SA winter by positioning indoor golf as the obvious choice when outdoor courses go cold.
brief.audience: Regular Jo'burg golfers who stop playing in winter because their home course gets cold or they travel less. They already have clubs — they just need a reason to keep playing.
brief.bigIdea: Winter doesn't exist in here. (It's always 22°C, there's food and drinks, and the simulator never closes.)
brief.successMetric: Winter session bookings vs prior year. Secondary: winter package upsells. Tertiary: social engagement on contrast-style content.
brief.whatGoodLooksLike: A visual that makes you want to be inside — warm lights, green fairways on screen, something cold and grey outside the window. A hook that names the weather or the day. Content that feels like a friend saying 'actually, this is good.'
brief.whatBadLooksLike: Clinical data overlays. Golf swing technique photos. Anything that makes indoor golf sound like a chore or a substitute. Content that positions winter as a problem rather than Swing Shack as the answer.

dna.tone: Warm, inviting, slightly cheeky. The tone of a friend who knows the best spot in Jo'burg. Not trying to be premium or clinical — just genuinely fun. Think: 'you know what this weather needs? A round.'
dna.contentMix: 40% social proof (look how good it is inside) / 30% contrast/humor (cold vs warm) / 20% practical (sessions available, deals) / 10% lifestyle (food, drinks, atmosphere)
preferredVisualStyles: cozy bar/food setup at Swing Shack
contrast: grey sky outside vs green simulator inside
forbiddenVisualStyles: cold blue colour grading on indoor content
anything that makes indoor golf look like a chore
dna.ctaPhilosophy: Casual and low-friction: 'Book a session' not 'Book now — limited slots.' Make it feel like a no-brainer, not a sales push.

platformStrategy.instagram: Lifestyle-first: food, drinks, simulators, social vibe. Contrast hooks work well. Carousels showing 'inside vs outside' perform.
platformStrategy.tiktok: 'It's [X]°C outside. This is what we did instead.' Fast, relatable, shareable. Show the vibe, not the data.
platformStrategy.gmb: Seasonal/event posts. 'Winter sessions available.' Warm imagery, social proof. 'Book your winter round.'

strategy.positioningStatement: When the courses go cold, the simulator doesn't.
strategy.targetAudience: Regular Jo'burg golfers who play less in winter. They love golf but the weather stops them.
strategy.primaryOffer: Winter sessions from R250. Winter package deals available.

brief.audience: Johannesburg golfers who are using ill-suited clubs, struggling with consistency, or looking to improve their game through better equipment choices.
brief.goalNotes: Drive practice session and fitting bookings by educating golfers on the importance of using the correct clubs for their swing, skill level, and playing style. Reinforce that the right equipment leads to better performance, consistency, and enjoyment on the course.
brief.context: Campaign theme: "You wouldn't dig a hole with a pool noodle. You wouldn't run a marathon in flip-flops. So why play golf with the wrong clubs?" Visual direction should compare obviously incorrect tools or equipment with golfers using unsuitable clubs. Focus on education, performance improvement, and the value of proper club selection and fitting.

strategy.positioningStatement: For Johannesburg golfers who are using ill-suited clubs, struggling with consistency, or looking to improve their game through better equipment choices. who want to Bookings.
strategy.targetAudience: Johannesburg golfers who are using ill-suited clubs, struggling with consistency, or looking to improve their game through better equipment choices.

pillars.name: The Absurd Comparison Hook — making the problem impossible to ignore
pillars.description: This pillar owns the jarring visual comparisons that force recognition. It creates the initial cognitive dissonance by showing obviously wrong tools alongside subtly wrong golf equipment, making golfers question their own setup without feeling attacked.

pillars.name: The Hidden Performance Cost — what ill-suited clubs actually steal
pillars.description: This pillar owns the educational revelation of how wrong equipment sabotages consistency, distance, and confidence. It explains the mechanics (lie angle, shaft flex, loft matching) in digestible terms so golfers understand WHY their game suffers.

pillars.name: The Johannesburg Reality — local relevance and peer recognition
pillars.description: This pillar owns the geographic and social proof that this is a real problem for real local golfers. It features Johannesburg courses, local swing types, and relatable playing conditions to make the campaign feel specific, not generic.

pillars.name: The Fitting Solution — the expert path to right equipment
pillars.description: This pillar owns the bridge between problem and offer. It positions professional fitting as the essential, accessible solution — not intimidating or expensive-feeling, but as logical as visiting a doctor when something's wrong.

pillars.name: The Transformation Proof — real results from right equipment
pillars.description: This pillar owns the payoff evidence: before/after stories, consistency improvements, golfer testimonials. It proves that the campaign's promise delivers real outcomes, making the booking CTA feel like a confident decision.

dna.tone: Sardonic yet sympathetic — the tone of a sharp-eyed friend who spots something obviously absurd and can't resist pointing it out, with genuine care wrapped in wry provocation.
dna.contentMix: 35% jarring comparison content / 30% educational revelation / 25% proof-of-problem stories / 10% direct booking CTA
preferredVisualStyles: bold typographic overlays on dark backgrounds
dna.ctaPhilosophy: The CTA should feel like the obvious next step after a revelation — not pushy but inevitable. 'Book Your Fitting' or 'Start Your Practice Session' should read as relief, not pressure.

platformStrategy.instagram: Use Reels for side-by-side comparisons with trending audio, Stories for poll questions that expose equipment assumptions, and carousel posts for educational mini-lessons on club selection.
platformStrategy.gmb: Feature the campaign's proof content in posts, use the comparison theme in cover photo suggestions, and ensure GMB posts directly address equipment-related review concerns.

visualDirection.mood: Provocative clarity — the electric moment of recognition when something obviously wrong becomes undeniable.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Visuals should open with jarring wrong-tool scenarios — a chef attempting to flip pancakes with a tennis racket, a golfer hitting a driver with the shaft bent like a pool noodle. Then pivot to the real subject: Johannesburg golfers mid-swing with clubs visibly wrong for their physique or swing type. The contrast between obviously absurd equipment and subtly wrong clubs should create cognitive tension. Dark, dramatic lighting on the golfer creates gravitas; bright, clean lighting on the absurd comparison creates comic recognition. Gold emerges only in the 'solution moment' — the properly fitted club, the satisfied golfer, the booking button.
imageReferences: a chef trying to flip pancakes with a tennis racket, shot in a luxury kitchen with dramatic side-lighting
a marathon runner mid-race in flip-flops, sweat-drenched, on a city street in Johannesburg

a split-screen: left side shows a golfer with obviously wrong club (too long, wrong lie angle) mid-swing with visible struggle; right side shows the same golfer with properly fitted clubs, smooth release, confident finish
a close-up of two clubheads side by side — one with visible wear on the sole from incorrect turf interaction, one pristine and properly matched
a Johannesburg golfer looking frustrated at their shot, then cutting to the same golfer smiling on the green after a successful putt
visualDirection.colorUsage: The dark background (#0D0D0F) creates dramatic contrast that makes the problem feel serious, not silly — it elevates the campaign from joke to insight. The warm orange (#FF6B35) appears on text and elements that highlight the PROBLEM, creating urgency and drawing the eye to what's wrong. Gold (#D4AF37) is reserved exclusively for the SOLUTION moments — the correctly fitted club, the booking CTA, the satisfied golfer — creating a visual reward pathway that subconsciously links gold to relief.
visualDirection.typography: Bold, sans-serif typefaces with high legibility for social scrolling — think athletic brand aesthetics meets editorial boldness. Headlines should feel like provocative statements, not questions. The 'reveal' text (solution) can use a slightly refined serif to signal premium expertise.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Split-screen compositions are the campaign's signature — left side contains the problem (wrong equipment/absurd comparison), right side contains the context (golf course, golfer, Johannesburg setting). Generous negative space around subjects creates breathing room and focus. Text overlays should be minimal, punchy, and positioned to guide the eye through the comparison narrative.
contentExamples: Reel: 'POOL NOODLE vs YOUR DRIVER' — rapid cuts of obviously wrong tools, then pivot to a golfer struggling with wrong loft, text overlay: 'Still using last decade's clubs?'
Carousel: 5 slides showing common equipment mistakes Johannesburg golfers make, each with a 'Sound familiar?' hook, final slide books to fitting
Story series: Document a golfer's frustration with slice, reveal it's equipment-related, show the fitting process, end with their first clean strike
GMB post: Before/after swing analysis graphic with caption about how equipment changes game consistency, CTA to book practice session
Educational graphic: '3 signs your clubs are wrong for you' — inconsistent contact, adjustable hosels maxed out, clubs that don't match your height

platformStrategy.instagram: Use carousel slides for the comparison format — absurd tool on slide 1, wrong club parallel on slide 2, solution on slide 3. Reels should open with a deadpan visual hook in the first 1.5 seconds.

visualDirection.mood: Dark theatre with a spotlight moment — dramatic contrast that makes the solution feel golden and inevitable.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Visuals open in near-darkness with a single warm spotlight on the subject. The comparison imagery places an obviously absurd tool — a children's plastic toy shovel, flip-flops on a track — alongside a golfer using clearly wrong clubs on the course. The contrast is shot with equal visual weight so neither feels more ridiculous than the other, making the parallel undeniable. When the 'solution' appears — properly fitted clubs, a clean fitting bay, the golfer's confident follow-through — the palette shifts: the dark background remains but a wash of gold (#D4AF37) floods the frame, signaling the payoff. Every visual should feel like the moment before someone says 'Oh, THAT'S my problem.'
imageReferences: a golfer mid-swing in a dimly lit range with a club visibly too long for their frame, overhead angle, dramatic shadow
a split composition: left side shows a pool noodle poking through sand, right side shows the same golfer's club sole digging into turf at the same absurd angle
a fitting bay bathed in warm gold light with a fitted iron set arranged cleanly, the golfer's shoes and gloves visible in the foreground frame
a data overlay on a phone screen showing swing path before and after fitting — the 'after' path glowing in #D4AF37
a close-up of a clubhead striking a ball with motion blur, the ball flight traced with a thin gold line
visualDirection.colorUsage: The dark background (#0D0D0F) creates dramatic theatre — it forces the eye to focus only on what matters and makes the warm orange (#FF6B35) pop like an alarm clock going off. This is deliberate: the orange signals 'wake up, something is wrong.' The gold (#D4AF37) is reserved exclusively for the solution — it should feel earned, like the lights coming up after a revelation. White text on dark backgrounds maximises readability and maintains the high-contrast, almost cinematic feel of the campaign. Never use orange and gold simultaneously — they must not compete; orange is the problem signal, gold is the answer signal.
visualDirection.typography: Bold, condensed sans-serif for headlines — think impact without decoration. Use uppercase for comparison callouts ('WRONG TOOL FOR THE JOB') to create visual punch. Body copy in a clean, readable sans-serif with generous tracking for a premium feel. Avoid serif fonts entirely — they add warmth this campaign deliberately withholds until the gold moment.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Grid-based, high-contrast layouts with generous negative space. The dark background should dominate — content occupies no more than 40% of the frame. Use a strict two-zone layout for comparison posts: absurdity on the left, golf reality on the right, divided by a thin #FF6B35 line. The gold accent appears only as a border, icon fill, or highlight — never as a background fill.
contentExamples: Side-by-side carousel: 'You wouldn't paint a wall with a toothbrush' / 'So why are you playing with clubs 2 inches too long?' — ends with Book a Practice Session CTA
Reel: Silent 6-second clip of a golfer shanking a shot, followed by a 2-second intertitle 'Wrong clubs?' then the same golfer striping a iron after a fitting — tagged with Johannesburg location
GMB post: '5 signs your clubs are wrong for your swing — and what a fitting actually fixes.' Short text post with a booking link.

pillars.name: The Absurdity Parallel — Making the Problem Impossible to Ignore
pillars.description: Owns the campaign's core hook: using obviously wrong everyday tools as a mirror for wrong golf equipment. Every piece of content under this pillar opens with a comparison that makes the golfer feel seen and slightly uncomfortable in a productive way. This pillar drives initial awareness and scroll-stopping power.

pillars.name: The Swing Truth — Data-Proven Consequences of Wrong Clubs
pillars.description: Owns the educational proof layer: why wrong clubs actually damage your swing mechanics, consistency, and distance. Uses swing data, ball flight patterns, and coaching evidence to transform the 'aha moment' into a credible, data-backed argument. This pillar builds trust and positions the brand as technically credible.

pillars.name: The Fitting Process — Making the Unknown Known
pillars.description: Owns process transparency and removes the barrier of uncertainty. Shows exactly what a club fitting session looks like, how long it takes, what gets measured, and what the outcome is. This pillar converts awareness into intent by eliminating the 'I don't know what I'm signing up for' hesitation.

pillars.name: The Transformation Proof — Real Johannesburg Golfers, Real Results
pillars.description: Owns social proof and emotional resonance. Features real Johannesburg golfers sharing their before/after experience — what they were struggling with, what changed after fitting, and what it felt like to finally play with clubs built for them. This pillar makes the campaign feel local, relatable, and real.

pillars.name: The Urgency Catalyst — This Season, With These Clubs
pillars.description: Owns the final push from awareness to booking. Creates time-bound relevance — seasonal events, upcoming tournaments, the start of a new golfing year — and ties equipment correctness to immediate performance goals. This pillar is the campaign's conversion engine, driving clicks to Book a Practice Session.

visualDirection.mood: Confrontational clarity that dissolves into confident possibility — like flipping a light switch in a dark room.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Every visual opens with an obvious absurdity — a person using a garden hose as a tennis racket, a chef cutting with a butter knife — before cutting to a golfer using clubs that are plainly wrong for their swing: too long, too stiff, wrong loft. The contrast should be visceral and immediate. Then the visual transitions: the same golfer, same moment, with properly fitted clubs — their posture relaxes, the strike is clean, the result is satisfying. The gold accent appears ONLY in the moment of correct equipment — it marks the solution. The dark background should feel like a spotlight moment, pulling all focus to the subject.

Open with images that feel WRONG—a chef trying to flip pancakes with a putter, a surgeon reaching for a 3-iron instead of a scalpel, a golfer slicing with clubs clearly too long for their frame. Then pivot hard to the gold-accented solution moment: a perfectly struck iron, a fitted club in hand, a golfer's face showing genuine confidence. The contrast must be immediate and undeniable. Dark backgrounds make the orange urgency pop and the gold solution glow like a beacon. Avoid subtlety—every visual should communicate 'this is obviously wrong, and the fix is obvious too.'
imageReferences: a split-screen: left side shows a person hammering a nail with a putter, right side shows proper hammer in use
a golfer mid-swing with an obviously too-long driver overlaid with a red X and swing plane data
close-up of hands gripping a club with the shaft visibly bending, next to properly fitted grip
a Johannesburg skyline silhouette with the phrase 'Wrong clubs don't care about your handicap' in bold orange
visualDirection.colorUsage: The deep black background (#0D0D0F) creates theatrical darkness that makes every element feel intentional and dramatic—it's the stage for the 'obvious wrongness' reveal. Warm orange (#FF6B35) functions as a warning signal, the visual equivalent of saying 'stop, look at this'—it should appear on the absurd comparisons and problem indicators. Gold (#D4AF37) ONLY appears at the moment of solution, making it feel like the earned reward after acknowledging the problem. White text ensures legibility against the dark backdrop while maintaining the stark, high-contrast aesthetic.
visualDirection.typography: Bold, sans-serif type with heavy weight for headlines—think condensed athletic fonts or industrial stencil styles that feel direct and unapologetic. Body text should be clean and readable, contrasting with the aggressive headlines to guide the eye from problem to solution.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Split compositions that force comparison are essential—visuals should literally show wrong vs. right, before vs. after, without requiring mental effort from the viewer. Generous negative space around key messages prevents visual clutter and maintains the sharp, editorial feel.
contentExamples: Reel: 15-second sequence of absurd equipment swaps (spoon as putter, rake as driver) cutting to a golfer's face, then the same golfer with properly fitted clubs smiling after a pure strike
Carousel: '5 Signs Your Clubs Are Holding You Back' — each slide pairs a problem visual with a data point about swing inefficiency, final slide leads to booking CTA
Static post: Full-bleed image of a pool noodle next to a driver with text overlay 'Same result. Wrong tool.' — caption explains why shaft flex matters

pillars.name: The Absurdity Mirror — making the wrong obvious
pillars.description: Owns the moment of recognition. Uses wildly relatable non-golf comparisons (pool noodle, flip-flops, butter knife) to hold up a mirror to the absurdity of using ill-suited clubs. Every piece of content here should trigger a 'wait, that's actually ridiculous' response that opens the mind to change.

pillars.name: The Swing Truth — data-driven discomfort
pillars.description: Owns the educational credibility. Delivers concrete evidence that wrong equipment creates swing compensations—loss of distance, inconsistency, higher scores. Uses before/after data, swing plane analysis, and ball flight comparisons to make the problem measurable and undeniable.

pillars.name: The Johannesburg Proof — local transformation stories
pillars.description: Owns social proof and relatability. Features real Johannesburg golfers (handicap badges, local course references) who experienced dramatic improvement after fitting. Their stories validate the campaign's core argument through lived experience rather than abstract claims.

pillars.name: The Fitting Reveal — showing the solution
pillars.description: Owns the transformation process. Demystifies club fitting by showing what happens during a session—launch monitor data, shaft options, lie angle adjustments. Makes the booking decision feel informed rather than risky by demonstrating exactly what the golfer gains.

pillars.name: The Right Club Payoff — celebrating the fix
pillars.description: Owns the emotional reward. Shows the moment a golfer hits a pure shot with properly fitted clubs—the feel, the flight, the confidence. This pillar delivers the satisfaction payoff that makes the entire campaign arc feel complete and worth acting on.

This pillar builds desire for the practice session by framing the booking as the beginning of a discovery journey — a 30-minute session that reveals something fundamental about the golfer's game they didn't know.

pillars.name: Johannesburg Course Confidence — The Local Reality
pillars.description: This pillar owns geographic and social proof for the Johannesburg audience. It grounds the campaign in local context — specific Johannesburg course conditions, altitude affecting ball flight, the pressure of playing with members who have fitted clubs — making the campaign feel relevant, local, and urgent. This pillar converts the general awareness from pillars 1-3 into a Johannesburg-specific reason to act now.

pillars.name: The Right Equipment Reveal — Gold Moment Booking
pillars.description: This pillar owns the conversion moment. Every content piece ends here — the gold-accented reveal where fitted clubs and a confident golfer appear, and the CTA to book a practice session becomes impossible to ignore. This pillar is the emotional payoff of the entire campaign: the moment the audience thinks 'Okay, I get it. I need to do this.' It converts awareness into action through a single, specific, frictionless booking ask.

The contrast should make viewers wince with recognition. Dark, moody backgrounds with high-contrast subject isolation make the orange urgency pop and the gold solution moment feel earned. No soft gradients. No pleasant pastels. This is confrontation that ends in relief. Text overlays should be bold and minimal, in white on dark, with the gold accent reserved exclusively for the solution or CTA moment — never wasted on decorative elements.
imageReferences: a golfer lining up a shot with a pool noodle tucked under their arm, standing on a fairway at sunset, looking confused
a split-screen: left side shows a golfer topping every shot with a shaft clearly too stiff and too short, right side shows the same golfer smiling after a professional fitting session
a close-up of a club lying on dark turf with an orange light bar cutting across the image, highlighting the clubface angle — no golfer in frame, just the evidence of a bad fit
a dramatic overhead shot of a driving range mat with six mismatched clubs laid out in a row, each one obviously wrong for a different swing type, dark background with spotlight on the centre club
a candid-style photo of a Johannesburg golfer mid-swing indoors under studio lights, expression showing genuine frustration, with orange and gold colour grading on their grip
visualDirection.colorUsage: The dark background (#0D0D0F) creates the serious, confrontational stage — it says 'this is a real problem worth looking at.' The warm orange primary (#FF6B35) functions as the urgency signal, used sparingly on key contrast elements or text callouts to make the absurd comparison feel alive. The gold accent (#D4AF37) is sacred — it appears ONLY at the moment of solution, on the CTA, on the fitting imagery, or on the post-fitting smile, acting as the emotional reward for attention. White text on dark ensures maximum readability and authority. This palette is designed to move the viewer from discomfort (dark + orange) to aspiration (gold) in a single scroll.
visualDirection.typography: Bold, condensed sans-serif for headlines — punchy and slightly aggressive to match the provocative tone. Clean, regular weight sans-serif for body copy — readable and trustworthy. No serifs, no script fonts. Think sports editorial meets professional fitting studio. Headlines should be short and direct, like a coach calling out a bad decision.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Full-bleed dark backgrounds dominate. Asymmetric layouts preferred — the subject placed off-centre with negative space that builds tension. Gold elements always bottom-right or centred as the visual anchor. Consistent left-aligned text blocks on carousels. No centre-aligned body text — it reads too soft for this campaign's voice.
contentExamples: Reel: 'You wouldn't change a tyre with a spoon. So why are you playing with clubs that fight your swing?' Cut from tyre-change-with-spoon to golfer missing a short putt.

Carousel (5 slides): Slide 1 — Question: 'Why do you top the ball?' Slides 2-4 — Common causes: wrong shaft flex, wrong lie angle, wrong grip size. Slide 5 — 'Book a fitting and find out which club actually belongs in YOUR bag.'
GMB Post: 'After 12 years with the same off-the-rack driver, Michael finally got fitted. His drives are 20 yards longer and straighter. Read his story — link in bio.'

Reel: Split-screen slow-mo — left: golfer using a club 2 inches too short, stooping awkwardly. Right: same golfer after a custom fitting, standing tall, crisp contact. No narration, text on screen only.

pillars.name: The Absurd Comparison Hook — mismatch as obvious absurdity
pillars.description: This pillar owns the campaign's entry point — it makes the viewer laugh or wince by comparing obviously wrong equipment choices (pool noodle, flip-flops) to the golfer's own ill-suited clubs. It creates instant recognition and lowers defences to education. Every piece of content must earn attention through this contrast before it can deliver value.

pillars.name: The Swing Sabotage Story — equipment is the hidden villain
pillars.description: This pillar owns the educational argument that wrong equipment actively damages performance, consistency, and enjoyment — not just mildly impacts them. It shifts blame from the golfer's skill to the tool, reducing guilt and increasing openness to the fitting solution. Uses swing data, ball flight patterns, and relatable struggle scenarios to make the case.

pillars.name: The Honest Self-Assessment — are YOUR clubs right?
pillars.description: This pillar owns the introspective moment — it asks the golfer to honestly evaluate whether their current clubs match their swing speed, skill level, and playing goals. It creates cognitive dissonance without shaming, positioning the practice session as a path to clarity rather than a confession of failure. Designed to be shared or bookmarked as a self-diagnostic tool.

pillars.name: The Fitting Promise — custom as performance unlock
pillars.description: This pillar owns the solution — it positions a professional practice session and fitting as the definitive answer to the equipment problem established in the previous pillars. Content here is warm, expert, and outcome-focused. It sells confidence in the process, not just the transaction. Every CTA points here.

pillars.name: The Johannesburg Proof — local results from local golfers
pillars.description: This pillar owns social proof specific to the Johannesburg market — local golfer testimonials, before/after swing comparisons, and fitting outcomes from nearby courses and ranges. It grounds the campaign in real, relatable results and builds trust for the booking action. Geographic specificity is key — this isn't generic golf content.

dna.contentMix: 30% Problem-Awareness / 25% Educational / 25% Social Proof / 20% Conversion
dna.ctaPhilosophy: The CTA should feel like a door opening, not a push. 'Book Your Fitting' is the invitation to solve the problem you've just been shown. Every CTA carries the weight of the revelation that came before it.

platformStrategy.instagram: Use carousel posts for the comparison narrative—swipe to reveal the 'wrong club' vs 'right club' moment. Stories for real-time fitting bookings and golfer Q&As. Reels deliver the visual punch with fast-cut comparison clips.
platformStrategy.tiktok: Not applicable for this campaign.
platformStrategy.gmb: Use the Posts feature to publish educational comparison content and booking CTAs directly in GBP. Respond to reviews by reinforcing the equipment-fit message, making every interaction a micro-campaign touchpoint.

visualDirection.mood: Awakening in a spotlight. The moment you see the truth and it changes everything.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Visuals should open on the ABSTRACT—the pool noodle, the flip-flops, the clearly wrong tool—then SWIFTLY REVEAL its golf equivalent. A split-screen layout showing someone attempting a marathon in flip-flops on the left, transitioning or overlaid with a golfer playing a driver three times too stiff on the right. The contrast must be immediate and visceral. Dark, cinematic backgrounds with sharp lighting should frame each comparison, creating a 'forensic analysis' feel—almost like a crime scene investigation into why your scores won't drop. Gold appears only in the resolution: the correctly fitted club, the satisfied golfer, the solution moment. No smiley stock golfers. Real faces, real frustration, real relief.
imageReferences: a golfer gripping a club clearly too heavy for them, grimacing mid-swing in a dark indoor bay
split-screen: marathon runner in flip-flops vs golfer playing an overly stiff shaft, same body language of struggle
a clubface impact close-up with motion blur, shot on dark background, gold light catching the club head at the moment of truth
before-after: a Johannesburg golfer's inconsistent scorecard beside a clean, improving one after a fitting
visualDirection.colorUsage: The near-black background (#0D0D0F) creates the stage for the comparison drama—every other element pops against it. The warm orange (#FF6B35) acts as a warning light, used on problem elements (the wrong tool, the struggle shot, the frustrated face) to trigger instinctive recognition. Gold (#D4AF37) is rationed strictly for the solution—the fitted club, the booking button, the satisfied result—making it feel earned and premium. White text sits on the dark canvas for maximum legibility and editorial authority. This palette turns every post into a visual argument: problem in orange, stage in black, solution in gold.
visualDirection.typography: Headlines in bold condensed sans-serif (Impact-style) for maximum punch and instant recognition in a scroll-stop moment. Body copy in clean geometric sans-serif (Montserrat or similar) to maintain readability on dark backgrounds and project precision. Size contrast between headline and body should be aggressive—headlines LARGE, body small.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Split-panel and side-by-side layouts dominate. The screen should be divided visually to house the comparison tension—wrong vs right, before vs after, problem vs solution. Strong horizontal dividers and bold color blocks. Gold accents used as thin rule lines or small badges, never as large fills, so they feel like a finishing detail on a precision instrument.
contentExamples: Reel: 'You wouldn't dig a hole with a pool noodle. So why play golf with the wrong clubs?' — cut between absurd comparisons and real golfer swing struggles, 15 seconds
Carousel: '5 signs your clubs are holding you back' — slide 1: the hook, subsequent slides: specific symptoms with a fitting CTA on the final slide
GMB Post: 'The fitting room reveal — what most Johannesburg golfers discover on their first session.' Short educational text post with booking CTA button

pillars.name: The Absurdity Mirror — naming the silent problem
pillars.description: Owns the initial hook and problem recognition. This pillar uses the comparison logic (pool noodle / flip-flops / wrong tool) to make golfers suddenly see their own equipment mismatch as equally absurd. Every post under this pillar opens eyes first, creates the cognitive dissonance that drives all downstream action.

pillars.name: The Hidden Cost — what's wrong equipment stealing from your game
pillars.description: Owns the emotional depth of the campaign. Explores what inconsistency, lost distance, sliced shots, and plateaued scores actually cost a golfer—financially, emotionally, competitively. This pillar turns the abstract problem into personal stakes, making the fitting feel necessary rather than optional.

pillars.name: The Science of Fit — how club-swing connection works
pillars.description: Owns the educational credibility of the campaign. Breaks down shaft flex, clubhead design, lie angle, and grip size in accessible, jargon-free terms. Positions the practice session not as a sales pitch but as a diagnostic process—giving golfers a language to understand why their equipment matters and trust the solution.

pillars.name: Real Johannesburg Stories — transformations you can believe
pillars.description: Owns social proof and trust. Features local Johannesburg golfers who discovered their clubs were working against them and saw measurable improvement after a proper fitting. Grounded, specific, relatable—not celebrity endorsements but everyday golfers whose experience mirrors the audience.

pillars.name: The Right Fit Call-to-Action — book your session now
pillars.description: Owns the conversion moment and closes the campaign loop. Every post, story, and content piece funnels here. The CTA doesn't sell aggressively—it extends the invitation to discover the truth about your clubs. Urgency comes from the recognition already built, not from artificial scarcity.

This pillar translates the comedy into empathy — 'this is why you feel that way.' Converts amusement into personal relevance.

pillars.name: The Right Reality — showing what correct equipment enables
pillars.description: Owns the aspirational proof: what happens when clubs match your swing, speed, and style. Smooth contact, confidence over the ball, shots that curve intentionally. This pillar provides the hope and makes the gold colour feel like a destination worth reaching.

pillars.name: The Fitting Bridge — making professional fitting the obvious solution

Positions the fitter as a guide, not a salesperson. Makes booking feel like a smart choice, not a luxury.

pillars.name: The Practice Proof — reinforcing that sessions complete the transformation
pillars.description: Owns the final conversion layer: once properly fitted, practice sessions become the accelerant that makes the new equipment pay off. Positions the practice session as where the theory becomes feel, where fitted clubs become trusted tools. Completes the journey from awareness to booking.

visualDirection.mood: Provocative clarity — the moment the penny drops, the moment the wrong thing suddenly looks obviously wrong.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Visuals should open on the absurd — a person attempting a task with comically wrong equipment, shot dramatically and cleanly. Then a sharp, fast cut reveals a golfer on a course doing the exact same thing metaphorically: using a senior flex shaft on a high-swing-speed player, or a driver with the wrong loft for their attack angle. The contrast between the obviously ridiculous and the quietly accepted should feel jarring. Gold-toned club detail shots should appear as the moment of revelation — the 'right' equipment presented with reverence, clean lighting, and a sense of quiet power. Dark backgrounds throughout to let the orange urgency and gold solution moments pop with maximum impact.

visualDirection.mood: Late-night comedy meets early-morning range session — smart, slightly irreverent, undeniably logical.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Visuals should open with the absurd comparison — a pool noodle as a shovel, marathon runners in flip-flops, someone using a teaspoon to paint a house — then transition to the golf equivalent: a weekend golfer struggling with clubs entirely wrong for their swing speed or physical build. The contrast between ridiculous non-golf scenarios and relatable golf frustrations creates the 'aha' moment. Dark backgrounds make the warm orange pop during the problem framing, while gold appears only when presenting the solution — proper fitting and the right equipment. Swing footage should be overlaid with data graphics showing dispersion patterns, distance loss, or inconsistency metrics.

data visualization overlay showing shot dispersion maps — chaotic cluster with wrong clubs, tight pattern with proper clubs
visualDirection.colorUsage: The dark background (#0D0D0F) creates gravitas and makes the content feel premium and serious — this isn't just humor, it's important. Warm orange (#FF6B35) is reserved exclusively for problem-framing moments: the absurd comparisons, the 'ouch' realizations, the tension-building. Gold (#D4AF37) appears only in solution moments: the fitting process, the right clubs, the transformation — it signals value, expertise, and the reward. This creates a visual promise: orange means 'this is your problem,' gold means 'this is your answer.'
visualDirection.typography: Bold, confident sans-serif for headlines — punchy and immediate. Clean body text with high legibility for data and explanations. Numbers should be prominent in swing data overlays to lend scientific credibility to the equipment argument.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: High contrast split layouts work best — problem on left, solution on right. Heavy use of negative space around the orange problem elements. Gold accents should be contained to logos, CTAs, and solution imagery to create clear visual hierarchy.

pillars.description: Owns the 'aha moment' content — demystifying what club fitting actually is and why it matters. Shows the process, the technology, the expertise. Positions fitting as the solution discovered, not a service sold. Builds trust and removes objections.

pillars.name: The Transformation Proof — Real Results, Real Golfers
pillars.description: Owns social proof and credibility. Features Johannesburg golfers whose game changed after proper fitting. Shows measurable improvements, emotional reactions, and specific outcomes. Makes the abstract benefit concrete and local.

pillars.name: The Invitation — Book Your Practice Session
pillars.description: Owns the conversion moment. Every piece of content leads here — not as a hard sell but as the natural next step after revelation. Presents booking as the path to discovery, not just a transaction. Makes the CTA feel like self-improvement, not spending.

dna.tone: Sardonic yet sympathetic — the tone of a sharp-eyed friend who spots something obviously absurd and can't resist pointing it out, with genuine care wrapped in wry provocation.
dna.contentMix: 35% jarring comparison content / 30% educational revelation / 25% proof-of-problem stories / 10% direct booking CTA
preferredVisualStyles: bold typographic overlays on dark backgrounds
dna.ctaPhilosophy: The CTA should feel like the obvious next step after a revelation — not pushy but inevitable. 'Book Your Fitting' or 'Start Your Practice Session' should read as relief, not pressure.

platformStrategy.instagram: Use Reels for side-by-side comparisons with trending audio, Stories for poll questions that expose equipment assumptions, and carousel posts for educational mini-lessons on club selection.
platformStrategy.gmb: Feature the campaign's proof content in posts, use the comparison theme in cover photo suggestions, and ensure GMB posts directly address equipment-related review concerns.

visualDirection.mood: Provocative clarity — the electric moment of recognition when something obviously wrong becomes undeniable.
visualDirection.creativeDirection: Visuals should open with jarring wrong-tool scenarios — a chef attempting to flip pancakes with a tennis racket, a golfer hitting a driver with the shaft bent like a pool noodle. Then pivot to the real subject: Johannesburg golfers mid-swing with clubs visibly wrong for their physique or swing type. The contrast between obviously absurd equipment and subtly wrong clubs should create cognitive tension. Dark, dramatic lighting on the golfer creates gravitas; bright, clean lighting on the absurd comparison creates comic recognition. Gold emerges only in the 'solution moment' — the properly fitted club, the satisfied golfer, the booking button.
imageReferences: a chef trying to flip pancakes with a tennis racket, shot in a luxury kitchen with dramatic side-lighting
a marathon runner mid-race in flip-flops, sweat-drenched, on a city street in Johannesburg

a split-screen: left side shows a golfer with obviously wrong club (too long, wrong lie angle) mid-swing with visible struggle; right side shows the same golfer with properly fitted clubs, smooth release, confident finish
a close-up of two clubheads side by side — one with visible wear on the sole from incorrect turf interaction, one pristine and properly matched
a Johannesburg golfer looking frustrated at their shot, then cutting to the same golfer smiling on the green after a successful putt
visualDirection.colorUsage: The dark background (#0D0D0F) creates dramatic contrast that makes the problem feel serious, not silly — it elevates the campaign from joke to insight. The warm orange (#FF6B35) appears on text and elements that highlight the PROBLEM, creating urgency and drawing the eye to what's wrong. Gold (#D4AF37) is reserved exclusively for the SOLUTION moments — the correctly fitted club, the booking CTA, the satisfied golfer — creating a visual reward pathway that subconsciously links gold to relief.
visualDirection.typography: Bold, sans-serif typefaces with high legibility for social scrolling — think athletic brand aesthetics meets editorial boldness. Headlines should feel like provocative statements, not questions. The 'reveal' text (solution) can use a slightly refined serif to signal premium expertise.
visualDirection.layoutStyle: Split-screen compositions are the campaign's signature — left side contains the problem (wrong equipment/absurd comparison), right side contains the context (golf course, golfer, Johannesburg setting). Generous negative space around subjects creates breathing room and focus. Text overlays should be minimal, punchy, and positioned to guide the eye through the comparison narrative.
contentExamples: Reel: 'POOL NOODLE vs YOUR DRIVER' — rapid cuts of obviously wrong tools, then pivot to a golfer struggling with wrong loft, text overlay: 'Still using last decade's clubs?'
Carousel: 5 slides showing common equipment mistakes Johannesburg golfers make, each with a 'Sound familiar?' hook, final slide books to fitting
Story series: Document a golfer's frustration with slice, reveal it's equipment-related, show the fitting process, end with their first clean strike
GMB post: Before/after swing analysis graphic with caption about how equipment changes game consistency, CTA to book practice session
Educational graphic: '3 signs your clubs are wrong for you' — inconsistent contact, adjustable hosels maxed out, clubs that don't match your height

pillars.name: The Absurd Comparison Hook — making the problem impossible to ignore
pillars.description: This pillar owns the jarring visual comparisons that force recognition. It creates the initial cognitive dissonance by showing obviously wrong tools alongside subtly wrong golf equipment, making golfers question their own setup without feeling attacked.

pillars.name: The Hidden Performance Cost — what ill-suited clubs actually steal
pillars.description: This pillar owns the educational revelation of how wrong equipment sabotages consistency, distance, and confidence. It explains the mechanics (lie angle, shaft flex, loft matching) in digestible terms so golfers understand WHY their game suffers.

pillars.name: The Johannesburg Reality — local relevance and peer recognition
pillars.description: This pillar owns the geographic and social proof that this is a real problem for real local golfers. It features Johannesburg courses, local swing types, and relatable playing conditions to make the campaign feel specific, not generic.

pillars.name: The Fitting Solution — the expert path to right equipment
pillars.description: This pillar owns the bridge between problem and offer. It positions professional fitting as the essential, accessible solution — not intimidating or expensive-feeling, but as logical as visiting a doctor when something's wrong.

pillars.name: The Transformation Proof — real results from right equipment
pillars.description: This pillar owns the payoff evidence: before/after stories, consistency improvements, golfer testimonials. It proves that the campaign's promise delivers real outcomes, making the booking CTA feel like a confident decision.
